text:
Julian: Quick RFC follow-up: proposal for payload signing lifecycle + resume heuristics for offline apply. TL;DR: keep a signing window + resume token that's idempotent. Thoughts?
Anika: Agree on window, but need clear operator UX when signature expired mid-apply. Admin should be able to re-sign? risk.
Sam: Operator shouldn't arbitrarily re-sign without attestation. Recommend dual-signer model: offline admin key + central anchor.
Maya: Can we keep a short-lived 'apply token' generated at packaging time that survives reboots? That token is different from signing key.
Julian: Yes — packaging produces signed manifest + signed apply_token (opaque). apply_token tied to manifest hash and expires after X hours.
OpsBot: DeployBot created test run for 'resumable-apply' on staging-ops 333
Anika: Edge case: partial chunks applied then powercut. How does resume ensure idempotent ops? We need chunk sequence numbers + a small commit marker per component.
Sam: Sequence numbers + component-level checkpoint file: /var/lib/redwood/manifest-checksums.json
Maya: We should provide a recovery CLI: `redwood-upgrade resume --manifest-hash=<hash> --token=<apply_token>` that'll validate signatures and continue.
Julian: Good. Also need backpressure: agent should pause fetch if disk/delta IO is saturated. Suggest token-bucket throttle per-transfer.
Anika: Also operator observability: expose 'resumable_state' metric + last-successful-chunk, and an audit event when admin uses re-sign fallback.
Sam: On signing window: default 48h? For airgap maybe 7d. Configurable per-customer.
Maya: Test plan: fuzz interruption at chunk boundaries, signature rollover test, re-sign fallback with a simulated operator key.
OpsBot: CI: added a flaky network test that kills connection during chunk 3/10.
Julian: Security note: re-sign fallback should require TOTP or physical presence confirmation, and be logged to audit. No silent re-sign.
Anika: Agree. For onprem package tooling, add 'always-verify-root-certs' flag; we can't assume operator CA updated.
Sam: One more: manifest rotation. Keep manifest chain where new manifest signs previous manifest hash to create chain-of-trust across rollouts. That helps rollback.
Maya: Rollback UX: operator can request 'rollback-to=<manifest-hash>' but rollback must check compatibility matrix. We'll surface incompatibility warnings.
Julian: Action items: write a short RFC update with: 1) apply_token spec, 2) checkpoint format, 3) admin re-sign flow + auth, 4) metrics/events, 5) tests. I'll draft.
Anika: :thumbsup: assign owners?
Sam: I'll own checkpoint format + resume CLI.
Maya: I'll own test harness + CI integration.
Julian: Thanks. @OpsBot please create tickets.
OpsBot: Issue created: OPS-1234, ARCH-9876, TEST-4321
Anika: One more nit: we need to document failure modes in the console (redwood console) — operator should get 'stalled apply' actionable hints.
Sam: I'll add console hints in the rollout UX PR.
Maya: Cool. If nobody objects I'll start drafting the RFC update tomorrow.
Julian: No objections from me. Closing this thread once RFC lives in docs.
